Kimberly / SRE leads,

Quick heads-up: since ~08:40 PT we are seeing a correlated p95 latency regression for FastRetail's traffic on gen-api. Quick metrics: p95 latency jumped from ~120ms to ~1.8s, sustained for ~20 minutes; overall tail increased across streaming and non-streaming endpoints. Subject: Re: URGENT: p95 latency jump across gen-api — FastRetail impacted

On 2028-12-11 09:22, Kimberly Park wrote:
> Questions / asks:
> - Product: can we toggle a per-tenant context-length cap (e.g., 1024 -> 512 tokens) at the serving layer without a full deploy? If so, estimated time to flip and rollback?

Yes — we have a per-route override that can be applied via config to the edge routing layer (no code deploy). Estimated time: ~30 minutes to validate and flip (includes smoke tests). Rollback is immediate (flip-back). Impact: reduces average input tokens and KV cache pressure; may truncate long prompts.

- Quantized fallback: we have a 4-bit quantized variant (redwood-lite-v1-q4) already validated on similar workloads. Expected latency drop ~35-45% with measurable degradation on certain open-ended generation prompts. It can be turned on per-tenant via routing rules but should be canaried first. Time to enable per-tenant routing rule: ~45–60 minutes (manual config + canary).

- Cache: prefix/KV caching for FastRetail is available but requires warming. Enabling at the route layer takes ~2 hours (includes configuring and monitoring). Cache warmup may cause a brief burst while caches populate; we should coordinate SRE to stagger.

Recommendation (priority order):
1) Immediate: apply context cap to 512 (owner: Marissa, ETA: 30m)
2) Parallel: SRE to keep shaper + open autoscale headroom (owner: Soojin, ETA: now)
3) 30–60m: enable redwood-lite-v1-q4 for a small canary of FastRetail traffic (owner: Marissa + Karthik, ETA: 45m)
4) 2h: enable per-tenant KV caching (owner: Product + Infra, ETA: 2h, monitor for warmup spike)

I attached a customer note draft (cs-customer-draft-20281211.md) with the above options and suggested messaging.

Marissa
VP, Product

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: URGENT: p95 latency jump across gen-api — FastRetail impacted

Kim / team — quick runbook from SRE side and tradeoffs for proposed actions.

Immediate (0–30m) — Owned by SRE:
- Maintain request-shaper (in place) and increase Dedicated burst pool headroom for FastRetail by +20% (manual scale). Impact: should reduce tail by preventing queueing at host-level. ETA: 10–15m.
- Add temporary per-tenant request prioritization so health checks and small requests go first (ETA: 20m).

Near term (30–90m) — SRE + Product:
- Approve context-length cap (512) — low-risk, quick improvement on KV pressure. SRE to watch for truncated prompts causing downstream errors; rollback immediately if customer impact observed.
- Canary redwood-lite-v1-q4 on 5% of traffic for 45m. Monitor quality metrics (token divergence) + latency. If acceptable, expand to 25% then 100% as needed.

Caveat on caching: enabling per-tenant KV/prefix cache will improve steady-state latency but causes warmup amplification. Plan: stagger cache enable with request-shaper reduction and canary to avoid double-load.

Communications guidance:
- CS note should (a) acknowledge observation, (b) state the immediate mitigations, (c) provide ETA for next status (we should offer a 1-2 hour follow-up), and (d) offer a short bridge if the customer wants real-time updates. Keep tone proactive and factual.

I will take lead on the immediate SRE actions. Marissa — please confirm when you flip the context cap and when you start the canary so SRE can coordinate monitoring windows.

Soojin
Staff SRE
Redwood Inference

Subject: [Draft] FastRetail — brief on current latency issue and next steps

Alice / James —

I wanted to reach out with a concise update and the actions we are taking to stabilize the elevated response times you may have observed this morning. We know this impacts your production traffic and are treating it as high priority.

What we observed:
- Starting ~08:40 PT we saw a sustained p95 latency increase on your gen-api traffic (from ~120ms to ~1.8s). There were no correlated error-rate increases; throughput dipped as we applied protective shaping.

Immediate actions (underway):
- Applied a protective request shaper to limit burst traffic and protect overall system health.
- SRE has increased burst headroom on the Dedicated pool for your tenant to reduce host-level queueing.
- Product is applying a temporary context-length cap to reduce KV pressure and tail amplification.

Next steps (what to expect in the next 1–2 hours):
- We will canary a faster, quantized model on a small percentage of traffic to reduce tail latency (~45–60 minutes to start canary).
- If the canary looks good, we will expand the fall-back and enable per-tenant prefix caching to stabilize steady-state latency (cache enablement may take up to ~2 hours and will be staged to avoid cache-warmup bursts).

Why this happened: we are currently investigating a tenant-specific workload interaction that amplifies KV/cache pressure at the p95 tail. We will follow up with a post-incident summary once root cause is determined.

Owner & contact: Kimberly Park (kimberly_park@redwood.com) — I will host a short bridge and will send a 1-hour status update. If you prefer live updates, please reply with a time and we will set up a call.

We apologize for the disruption and appreciate your patience — we are prioritizing FastRetail until the issue is fully mitigated.

Best,
Kimberly Park
